title: Microsoft kills off unsuccessful AI features while merging its separate Copilot apps
slides: Why is Microsoft killing its own AI features?
It is merging separate Copilot apps into one.
The failed features were quietly used by few users.
Your workflow may change, but tools stay familiar.
Check your Copilot app update for merged experience.
thread_text:
1. Why the purge?

Microsoft is quietly merging its separate Copilot apps into one, signaling that the standalone versions failed to gain traction.

2. The silent killer

The abandoned features were barely used, yet their removal could silently reshape your daily workflow.

3. The hidden shift

While tools stay familiar, the merge may change how you access AI assistance—without you noticing until it's done.

4. The bigger picture

This consolidation hints at a broader strategy: Microsoft betting on a unified AI experience over scattered features.

5. Your next move

Check your Copilot app update today. Will you adapt to the merged experience, or seek alternatives?

instagram.caption:
Your separate Copilot apps are being merged into one — Microsoft confirmed the consolidation after the standalone versions quietly failed to gain traction.

The features being killed were barely used by anyone. That’s why the removal feels invisible at first. But the merge changes where you find AI help inside tools you already use every day — same buttons, different door. 🔄

If you create content, your workflow may shift without a warning — one day you’ll open the app and the old options are just… gone. 📉

Is your Copilot app updated yet? Check today before the merge hits you mid-project. 🗓️
